title: Workflow to Visualise Trait Dispersion and Assess Invasibility
text: invasimapr R package assess species trait invasiveness site invasibility visualising trait dispersion computing invasion fitness. package implements network invasibility framework decomposes invasion fitness abiotic suitability, niche crowding resident competition components, enabling spatially explicit predictions establishment probability potential invaders. core workflow consists eight steps: Prepare inputs – assemble community, trait environmental matrices occurrence data. Simulate invaders – generate hypothetical invader trait profiles resampling resident traits. Trait space crowding – compute Gower-based trait space, convex hull membership niche crowding. Resident modelling – fit generalised linear mixed models resident abundance derive standardised predictors. Sensitivity estimation – estimate trait-dependent slopes abiotic suitability, crowding competition. Invader prediction – project invaders resident model space. Invasion fitness – compute per-invader, per-site invasion fitness multiple model options (–E). Establishment probability – map fitness establishment probability using probit, logistic hard-threshold transforms.

what: Probabilistic establishment from invasion fitness — compute_establishment_probability
title: Probabilistic establishment from invasion fitness — compute_establishment_probability
text: Invasion fitness \(\lambda_{}\) integrates trait-space geometry (distances, overlaps, convex hulls, centroids) abiotic suitability (alignment invader traits local environment), niche crowding (overlap resident trait space weighted composition), resident competition (site saturation). compute_establishment_probability() maps \(\lambda_{}\) probabilities establishment using unified interface: Probit: \(P = \Phi(\lambda / \sigma)\), \(\sigma\) scalar, residual standard deviation fitted auxiliary model, cell-wise predictive standard deviation. Logistic: \(P = \mathrm{logit}^{-1}(\lambda / \tau)\), \(\tau\) scale parameter. Hard rule: \(P = (\lambda > 0)\), yielding binary map. lambda_is supplied, function builds standardized predictors using \(\lambda_{} = \gamma r^{(z)}_{} - \alpha C^{(z)}_{} - \beta S^{(z)}_{} + \kappa\).

title: Compute invasion fitness \(\lambda_{is}\) for multiple model options — compute_invasion_fitness
text: compute_invasion_fitness() evaluates invasion-fitness surface \(\lambda_{}\) sites (\(s\)) invaders (\(\)) using three standardized predictors: Abiotic suitability \(r^{(z)}_{}\) (alignment invader traits local environment), Niche crowding \(C^{(z)}_{}\) (overlap resident trait space, weighted composition), Resident competition \(S^{(z)}_{}\) (site-level saturation). text: Compute invasion fitness multiple model options invasion fitness computed : Option : \(\lambda_{} = r^{(z)}_{} - \alpha_i C^{(z)}_{}     - \beta_i S^{(z)}_{} + \kappa\) Option B: \(\lambda_{} = \theta_0 r^{(z)}_{} - \alpha_i C^{(z)}_{}     - \beta_i S^{(z)}_{} + \kappa\) Option C: \(\lambda_{} = \theta_i r^{(z)}_{} - \alpha_i C^{(z)}_{}     - \beta_i S^{(z)}_{} + \kappa\) Option D: \(\lambda_{} = \Gamma_{} r^{(z)}_{} - \alpha_{} C^{(z)}_{}     - \beta_i S^{(z)}_{} + \kappa\) Option E: \(\lambda_{} = \theta_0 r^{(z)}_{} - \alpha_i C^{(z)}_{}     + \beta_i^{(signed)} S^{(z)}_{} + \kappa\) calibrate_kappa = TRUE, offset chosen mean resident invasion fitness equals zero.

title: Compute invasion fitness \(\lambda_{is}\) for multiple model options — compute_invasion_fitness
code: ## --------------------------------------------------------------- ## Minimal reproducible example (toy dimensions, no real ecology) ## ---------------------------------------------------------------  ## S = number of sites, I = number of invaders S = 5 I = 3 set.seed(1)  ## r_is_z : intrinsic growth component ## rows = sites (s), columns = invaders (i) r_is_z = matrix(   rnorm(S * I),   nrow = S,   ncol = I,   dimnames = list(paste0("s", 1:S), paste0("i", 1:I)) )  ## C_is_z : crowding / competition component (same shape as r_is_z) C_is_z = matrix(   rnorm(S * I),   nrow = S,   ncol = I,   dimnames = dimnames(r_is_z) )  ## S_is_z : site-only environmental gradient ## generated per-site, then broadcast across invaders S_is_z = matrix(   rep(scale(rnorm(S)), each = I),   nrow = S,   ncol = I,   dimnames = dimnames(r_is_z) )  ## Invader-specific baseline parameters alpha_i = setNames(runif(I, 0.2, 1.0), colnames(r_is_z))  # baseline crowding sensitivity beta_i  = setNames(runif(I, 0.1, 0.5), colnames(r_is_z))  # strength of S effect  ## --------------------------------------------------------------- ## Option A: fixed gamma = 1, no S effect (kappa = 0) ## --------------------------------------------------------------- outA = compute_invasion_fitness(   r_is_z, C_is_z, S_is_z,   option      = "A",   alpha_i     = alpha_i,   beta_i      = beta_i,   theta0      = 1,   return_long = FALSE )  ## --------------------------------------------------------------- ## Option B: gamma shared across invaders (gamma = theta_0) ## --------------------------------------------------------------- outB = compute_invasion_fitness(   r_is_z, C_is_z, S_is_z,   option      = "B",   alpha_i     = alpha_i,   beta_i      = beta_i,   theta0      = 0.8,   return_long = FALSE )  ## --------------------------------------------------------------- ## Option C: invader-specific gamma_i ## --------------------------------------------------------------- theta_i = setNames(   runif(I, 0.5, 1.2),   colnames(r_is_z) )  outC = compute_invasion_fitness(   r_is_z, C_is_z, S_is_z,   option      = "C",   alpha_i     = alpha_i,   beta_i      = beta_i,   theta_i     = theta_i,   return_long = FALSE )  ## --------------------------------------------------------------- ## Option D: fully site-varying Gamma_is and alpha_is ## ---------------------------------------------------------------  ## gamma_is : site x invader matrix of density-dependence scalars ## constructed by repeating gamma_i across sites Gamma_is = matrix(   rep(theta_i, each = nrow(r_is_z)),   nrow = nrow(r_is_z),   ncol = ncol(r_is_z),   dimnames = dimnames(r_is_z) )  ## alpha_is : site x invader crowding sensitivity ## start from invader-specific alpha_i and allow small site-level variation alpha_is = matrix(   NA_real_,   nrow = nrow(r_is_z),   ncol = ncol(r_is_z),   dimnames = dimnames(r_is_z) )  for (j in seq_len(ncol(r_is_z))) {   alpha_is[, j] = alpha_i[j] }  ## Add site-level noise and enforce positivity. ## pmax() drops matrix attributes, so we re-wrap explicitly. alpha_is = {   tmp = pmax(     0,     alpha_is + matrix(       rnorm(length(alpha_is), 0, 0.1),       nrow = nrow(r_is_z),       ncol = ncol(r_is_z)     )   )   matrix(     tmp,     nrow = nrow(r_is_z),     ncol = ncol(r_is_z),     dimnames = dimnames(r_is_z)   ) }  outD = compute_invasion_fitness(   r_is_z, C_is_z, S_is_z,   option      = "D",   alpha_is    = alpha_is,   beta_i      = beta_i,   Gamma_is    = Gamma_is,   return_long = FALSE )  ## --------------------------------------------------------------- ## Option E: signed S effect (positive or negative beta_i) ## --------------------------------------------------------------- beta_signed_i = setNames(   rnorm(I, 0, 0.3),   colnames(r_is_z) )  outE = compute_invasion_fitness(   r_is_z, C_is_z, S_is_z,   option          = "E",   alpha_i         = alpha_i,   beta_signed_i   = beta_signed_i,   theta0          = 1,   return_long     = FALSE )

text: Let \(X_{js}\) observed resident counts \(\mu_{js}\) expected counts. "opportunity_penalty" Abundance penalty: \(S_s = \log(1 + \sum_j X_{js})\). "modelled_dominance" Model-based crowding: \(S_s = \log(1 + \sum_j \mu_{js})\). Requires mu_js. title: Summaries of invasion fitness: species invasiveness, trait effects, and site invasibility — summarise_invasiveness_invasibility
text: Invasion fitness \(\lambda_{}\) integrates structure trait space (distances, overlaps, convex hull, cloud centroid) abiotic suitability (alignment environment), niche crowding (overlap residents weighted composition), resident competition (site saturation). summarise_invasiveness_invasibility() collapses site--invader surface species-, trait-, site-level summaries using either probabilistic measure \(P(\lambda > 0)\) hard rule \(\{\lambda > 0\}\). Species invasiveness (per invader) summarises breadth establishment across sites: $$V_i = |S|^{-1} \sum_s \{\lambda_{} > 0\}$$ $$\tilde V_i = |S|^{-1} \sum_s P(\lambda > 0 \mid , s).$$ Site invasibility (per site) quantifies openness newcomers: $$V_s = ||^{-1} \sum_i \{\lambda_{} > 0\}$$ $$\tilde V_s = ||^{-1} \sum_i P(\lambda > 0 \mid , s).$$ Trait invasiveness scores invader traits explain variation invasiveness, using standardized slopes continuous traits ANOVA \(R^2\) categorical traits.
